chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Mufrad pilgrim: does he advance his Tawaf or delay it? He said, 'He advances it.' A man beside him said, 'But my Sheikh did not do that; when he arrived, he stayed in Fakh until the people went to Mina, then he went with them.' I said, 'Who is your Sheikh?' He said, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both).' I inquired about the man, and it turned out he was the half-brother of Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) from the mother's side.
As for that which indicates what we mentioned, that the renewal of the Talbiyah was commanded only so that a person does not enter while being in the state of Ihram, what was narrated:

key_terms.مُحِلًّا: In the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.مُفْرِدِ الْحَجِّ: Mufrad pilgrim (one who performs Hajj only, without Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mufrad pilgrim regarding the timing of Tawaf upon arrival in Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural preference for Mufrad pilgrims to perform Tawaf al-Qudum immediately upon arrival, as instructed by Imam al-Baqir. The narration highlights the scholarly nuance of *ikhtilaf* (divergence) within the Ahl al-Bayt tradition, validating the practice of delaying Tawaf until after Mina as a legitimate alternative practiced by the Imam’s own half-brother, thereby demonstrating the flexibility in ritual timing within Shia fiqh.
